summary: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work, an agentic feature built on Codex and GPT-5.6 that can execute multi-step tasks across connected apps and files, alongside a merged desktop app with built-in browser, Computer Use, and Scheduled Tasks.

mechanisms.reason: The product shifts work from human-operated software to an agent that executes delegated, multi-step tasks autonomously across apps.
mechanisms.quote: ChatGPT Work is an agent that can take action across your apps and files, stay with a project for hours if needed, and turn a goal into finished work.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6 is claimed to improve multi-step reasoning and template-following, relevant to teams building reasoning-heavy or document-generation agents, but the claim is the lab's own and tied to a product launch rather than an independent benchmark.
practices.quote: GPT‑5.6 makes ChatGPT state of the art at reasoning through multi-step tasks and creating materials that follow your templates and reference files.

practices.reason: The design pattern of decomposing a goal into steps, running them independently with checkpoints and scheduled triggers, is a scaffolding approach engineering teams could adapt even though it is described as a vendor feature rather than an open technique.
practices.quote: stay with complex projects for hours by breaking them into smaller steps and completing them independently

practices.reason: The disclosed red-teaming result on the auto-review safeguard is an internal safety evaluation process, informative but not directly transferable to another team's stack.
practices.quote: During adversarial red teaming, auto-review blocked 100% of attempts to extract protected data, including attacks the reviewing model had not seen during training.

notable_reason: A major agentic product launch from OpenAI (ChatGPT Work) combined with a new frontier model rollout and a deprecation of the standalone Atlas browser, signaling a real shift toward agent-executed enterprise workflows.
